summary: California's last classic light station, finished in 1932 on East Anacapa, replaced a 1912 unattended beacon and was automated in 1968.

notes_for_editor: Keepers beyond the five principal keepers 1932-41 are not individually written up: USLHS roster lists ~85 lines through 1968, including post-1960 Coast Guardsmen (left out of the roster here). Names of the Coursey keeper vary: USLHS Charles R. (head keeper 1935-38, second/first assistant 1933-35), Bulletin 1934 C. H., NPS Rex; not linked beyond the Bulletin. The 1934 Bulletin issues are dated 1 Sept (rescue, PDF p.21) and 1 Dec (wife, p.29). The 1933-volume gale report is from December 1932 inferred from weekday/date in Cobb's log (9 Dec Fri). 1932 Bulletin OCR is garbled in places (four keepers' quarters, focal-plane height); 277 ft focal height is from NRHP/USLHS. Quarters 'for four keepers' read from OCR 'fdur'. The 1915 Commissioner report page (92) is for estimates for the following year. USCG Historian page blocked (403) so not used. Checker 2026-10-27: the gale report (Bulletin 1933 vol.) gives 'December 13' without a year, placed in December 1932 from the weekdays in the log; the fog-signal report's ship name and district number are OCR-garbled, so the story does not give them. NPS (1911 tower; fog signal 'hourly' crew of 15-25) and NRHP (original lens still in tower) differ from other sources in places; the story relies on NPS for the 1989 lens change.
